title: MiniMax Music 3, node by node
hook: The text encoder writes the song. Then a diffusion model performs it. Caption, lyrics, seconds and the 128-channel latent, from the source.

verified.claim: The text encoder runs an autoregressive model loop up to max_duration and returns one hidden vector per audio frame.
The node's seconds output is the length of that conditioning divided by 25, so it can come out shorter than max_duration.
9000 frames at 25 a second is the ceiling, 360 s.
The DAV decoder folds [B, 128, L] to [2B, 64, L], and it can't encode.
The DiT pads a short condition with zeros, and works in windows above 200 frames.
The lab's latent_length and prompt cleaning match the real functions on these inputs.
The README describes an 8B Global LLM, a 0.6B Local LLM, Flow Matching and Flow-VAE, and songs up to five minutes.
studio/music3_styles.json reports 19 families, 675 styles and 1056 cards.
The graph passes validate_prompt with its file menus skipped.
The licence's commercial terms ask for a prominent MiniMax-Music3 display in the product's interface, and separate written authorization above 20 million US dollars of yearly revenue.

unchecked: We did not run a render for this lesson. The clips are earlier renders in our gallery. The files there are shortened copies.
The advice on caption blocks, section tags and instrumentals comes from our skill notes, hand-tested on an older software stack with few seeds.
Mapping the README's two LLMs to the 36-layer main model and 4-layer audio_decoder in source is our reading. The README does not name the code.
Cost figures in our skill notes (about 1.7 to 2.1 times real time) are old-stack measurements and were not rerun.
MiniMax's README says the model produces 32 kHz audio, while ComfyUI's latent_length and VAE use 44100 Hz. We follow the code here and did not render to measure a raw file.
